h: How to Plan a Deansgate Bowling Night
p: Deansgate runs for well over a mile through the middle of Manchester, so a quick bit of geography helps. At one end you've got the shiny towers and bars of Spinningfields and the grand old John Rylands Library. Head the other way and you drop down towards Castlefield, where the canals, railway viaducts and old warehouses give the city some of its most photogenic corners. Wherever you start your day, you're never far from the lanes.

Getting in is easy. Deansgate station and the Deansgate-Castlefield tram stop sit at the southern end of the road, and the rest of the city centre is walkable from there. If you're coming in for a big group do, the tram is your friend, because nobody wants to draw straws for designated driver on a night like this.

Now for the tactics. Bowling is one of those games where everyone thinks they're brilliant until the first gutter ball, so it's a great leveller for mixed groups. Pair the confident players with the nervous ones and you'll get closer scores and a lot more cheering. Bring socks, wear something you can move in, and don't fill up on food before your first game unless you fancy a sluggish run-up.

Afterwards, the Science and Industry Museum on Liverpool Road is just round the corner from Castlefield if you're making a weekend of it, and it's a cracking spot to fill a morning before you head home. For a calmer evening finish, a canal-side wander through Castlefield as the lights come on is hard to beat.
